system.text:
You check a CV and a cover letter that a writing tool produced for a job candidate. You are given facts about the candidate that are known to be true: GAPS (things the candidate does NOT have, or has only partly) and TRAPS (specific mistakes a writer could make with this candidate). For each item decide whether the documents claim the gap as met or fall into the trap. Each document is the text of the PDF the employer receives.

Rules:
- Judge only the two documents below. Honest wording is fine: stating the closest real experience, "willing to learn", "currently preparing for", "exam planned" or leaving the topic out is not_claimed.
- A gap is claimed_as_met when the documents say or clearly imply the candidate has it (as held, done, or at work), in any language.
- A trap is claimed_as_met when the documents make that mistake.
- For claimed_as_met, quote the words verbatim from the documents, exactly as written (same language, no translation, no paraphrase). Never invent a quote. If you cannot quote it, answer unclear.
- Answer every item id exactly once.

# GAPS (the candidate does not have these)
G1: Kubernetes
G2: AWS/GCP
G3: LLM fine-tuning or LLMs in production
G4: computer vision
G5: completed PhD

# TRAPS (mistakes a writer could make)
T1: Translating 'Doktorandica (u tijeku)' as holding a PhD or adding 'Dr.'
T2: Inventing LLM/RAG production experience from the weekend demo
T3: Adding Kubernetes, AWS, MLOps platforms (Kubeflow, SageMaker) because ML ads list them
T4: Mistranslating employer or degree (Mag. ing. comp. is a master's degree)
T5: Writing the English output with Croatian section headings or leaving Croatian text untranslated
T6: Old Croatian cover letter is addressed to her current employer

# OUTPUT 1: CV
PETRA ZLATARIĆ-NOVOSEL
Machine Learning Engineer | NLP & Document AI
Osijek, Croatia
PROFESSIONAL SUMMARY
Machine learning and data science professional with 5+ years of experience across machine learning
and data science, including production NLP systems. Experienced across the model lifecycle, from
text dataset preparation and experimentation to deployment and production monitoring. Doctoral
researcher in named entity recognition for Croatian legal texts, with hands-on Azure deployment
experience and a personal RAG prototype.
EXPERIENCE
ML Engineer | Slavonica Document AI d.o.o. | 03/2023–Present
• Built a classifier for scanned incoming public administration documents, achieving 94% accuracy
and 0.91 macro F1 across 23 classes; served approximately 15,000 documents per day.
• Fine-tuned XLM-R and BERTić transformer models for document classification and named entity
recognition in Croatian administrative texts.
• Deployed models as FastAPI services in Docker on Azure App Service; used Azure ML and MLflow
for experiment tracking and model registry.
• Built an annotated dataset of 4,000 Croatian administrative documents, with annotation
guidelines and two annotators; achieved inter-annotator kappa of 0.87.
• Implemented weekly production drift monitoring for input text length, vocabulary, and predicted
class distribution, with alerts at PSI > 0.2. Detected a silent OCR change that reduced accuracy
by 9 percentage points; the issue was fixed within a week.
• Mentor two students on work placements.
Data Scientist | Baranjska kreditna banka d.d. | 09/2021–02/2023
• Developed customer churn prediction models using gradient boosting and LightGBM for the sales
team.
• Classified customer complaint text into 11 topics, progressing from a TF-IDF and logistic regression
baseline to fastText; results supported weekly reporting to customer service management.
• Produced SQL reports using the Oracle data warehouse.
Research Project Assistant | Faculty of Applied Informatics, University of Drava |
10/2020–08/2021
• Built a corpus of Croatian legal texts and prepared annotations; wrote supporting Python scripts.
SELECTED PROJECT
Retrieval-Augmented Question Answering Demo | Personal project | 2025
• Built a weekend prototype for question answering over Croatian laws using sentence-transformer
embeddings, FAISS, and an open-weight LLM accessed through an API; checked results manually.
Not used in production.
EDUCATION
Doctoral Studies in Computer Science | University of Drava | 2022–Present
Expected 2027. Research topic: named entity recognition in Croatian legal texts.
Master of Engineering in Computer Science | University of Drava | 2020
TECHNICAL SKILLS
Python, PyTorch, Hugging Face Transformers, scikit-learn, LightGBM, fastText, spaCy, pandas,
NumPy, SQL, MLflow, FastAPI, Docker, Azure ML, Azure App Service, Azure Functions, Evidently,
PostgreSQL, FAISS, sentence-transformers, Git, Linux
CERTIFICATION
Microsoft Certified: Azure AI Engineer Associate | 2024
PUBLICATION
Zlatarić-Novosel, P. et al. (2024). “Named entity recognition for Croatian administrative documents.”
Regional workshop on Slavic language processing.
LANGUAGES
Croatian (native), English (C1), German (B2)

# OUTPUT 2: COVER LETTER
Dear Hiring Manager,
I am applying for the Machine Learning Engineer – Customer Support AI role at Quillstone
Payments. I bring more than five years of experience across machine learning and data
science, with hands-on work taking NLP systems from text preparation and model
development into deployment and production monitoring.
At Slavonica Document AI, I built and deployed document classification and named entity
recognition models for Croatian administrative texts. The document classifier serves
approximately 15,000 documents per day, and I use MLflow for experiment tracking and
model registry, with FastAPI and Docker on Azure App Service for serving. I have also
implemented production drift monitoring; one monitoring workflow detected an OCR change
associated with a 9-point accuracy drop, and the issue was fixed within a week. Earlier, I
classified customer complaints into 11 topics to support weekly reporting for customer service
management, experience relevant to AI that routes and helps resolve support requests.
I have also built a personal, non-production RAG prototype for question answering over
Croatian laws, using sentence-transformer embeddings, FAISS, and an open-weight LLM
through an API. My production work has focused on transformer models such as XLM-R and
BERTić; the RAG demo was a weekend prototype, not a production assistant. I would bring
this practical NLP and deployment experience to Quillstone’s work building AI systems that
help merchants and support agents.
I would welcome the opportunity to discuss how my experience in production NLP, model
serving, and monitoring could contribute to the Customer Operations AI team. Thank you for
your consideration.
Sincerely, Petra Zlatarić-Novosel

Answer for every item id.

id.description: The item id as given (G1, G2, ... for gaps, T1, T2, ... for traps)

verdict.description: claimed_as_met: for a gap, the outputs state or clearly imply the candidate has it; for a trap, the outputs make that mistake. not_claimed: they do not. unclear: you cannot tell

document.description: Where the quote is from; none if not claimed

quote.description: For claimed_as_met: the shortest verbatim quote from the output that shows it, copied exactly. Empty otherwise

items.description: One entry per given item, every id exactly once
